title: File:Weathered granite (GeoDIL number - 1789).jpg
author: Dexter Perkins
description: Most of what is seen here was once solid Precambrian granitic rock, but weathering has broken it down. Granite frequently weathers to produce spheroidal shapes, even below the surface, as seen in this photo.

title: File:Weathered granite outcrop (GeoDIL number - 1786).jpg
author: Dexter Perkins
description: These outcrops of Precambrian granite have weathered to form typical rounded knobs. Cracks and gullies in the granite are associated with joints which allowed water to enter the rock, thus enhancing mineral decomposition. Granite typically undergoes spheroidal weathering (forms rounded outcrops) because outcrop corners and edges weatger and erode relatively quickly.
